blocks.text: Adding text in Photoshop on Mac takes about a minute once you know the two text modes. The typing is the easy part. Picking the right text mode is harder, and so is finding the controls that move when you switch tools. This page covers the Mac keys, the menu paths, and the places where people get stuck. The version details refer to Photoshop 27.6, the newest release our sources confirm, which came out in April 2026.
Point text or paragraph text: which one to use

Photoshop gives you two ways to place type with the Type tool. A single click creates point type. Point text does not wrap, so a line keeps going as far as you type it. Press Return to start a new line. Use point text for titles, labels and short phrases. A click and drag creates paragraph type inside a bounding box. Paragraph text wraps at the edge of the box, so you can write several sentences without breaking lines by hand.

rows: Press Return to start a new line
Option-click, then enter width and height
Text wraps to the size you set
blocks.caption: Point and paragraph type compared

blocks.text: A simple rule helps. Use point type for a short line that never needs to wrap. Drag a box when the words must fit a space you have already chosen. Julieanne Kost's tips, published in 2020, note that Option-click on a Mac sets the width and height of a fixed paragraph box with numbers. That helps when a layout needs exact dimensions, such as a banner with a fixed width.
Set font, size and color in the Options bar

When the Type tool is active, the Options bar sits at the top of the Photoshop window. It shows the controls for your text. You will see a font family menu, a style menu, a size field and a color swatch. Change them before you type if you already know what you want. You can also select the words first and change them after. Select only some characters if you want a change to touch part of the text. Leave everything selected if you want the whole block to change.

For finer control, open the Character panel with Window > Character. It holds leading, which is the space between lines. It also holds kerning and tracking, which control the space between characters. Tracking is the setting you will use most for headlines. On a Mac, Option plus the Left or Right Arrow key adjusts tracking without opening the panel.

Alignment works the same way. With the Type tool active, Command+Shift+L sets left alignment, Command+Shift+C sets center and Command+Shift+R sets right. Alignment controls how each line sits inside the text box, so it matters most for paragraph text and multi-line labels.
Commit, move and edit your text later

Text stays in edit mode until you commit it. Command+Return commits the text, and it is the key most people miss. Plain Return only starts a new line, so pressing it at the end of a headline does nothing useful. Clicking outside the text, or switching to another tool or layer, also commits it. The text layer is then ready to move, scale and style.

To move the text, press V for the Move tool and drag the layer. For rotation and scaling, use Edit > Free Transform or press ⌘T. Drag a corner handle to scale. Hold Shift while you drag a corner to keep the proportions. Press Return to apply the change, or Escape to cancel.

To edit text later, select its layer in the Layers panel and press T. Click inside the words to place the cursor. Double-click the T thumbnail on the layer to select every word. Fixing one typo this way beats retyping a whole headline when a client changes a single word.
Keyboard shortcuts for typing on a Mac

items: Command+Return commits the text. Plain Return starts a new line.
Command+Shift+L, C or R aligns text left, center or right.
Command+Shift+> or < changes the size by 2 pt. Add Option for 10 pt steps.
Option+Left or Right Arrow adjusts tracking.
Double-click the T thumbnail to select all text on that layer.

blocks.text: Learn three keys first. T opens the Type tool. Command+Return commits. Return starts a new line. Those three cover most of the work. Add the alignment and size shortcuts once the basics feel automatic. The size shortcuts move text in small steps, so use the 10 pt version when you need to cover a wider range of sizes quickly.
Common mistakes when adding text in Photoshop

The first mistake is pressing Return at the end of a paragraph box and expecting the text to commit. It starts a new line instead. Use Command+Return. The second mistake is clicking when you meant to drag. A single click creates point type, which runs off the edge of a narrow layout. The third mistake is switching tools mid-edit. Switching tools commits the text, so check the layer before you move on.

Sometimes the Type tool stops responding. One Adobe Community thread describes a text layer that could not be edited until a side panel was closed. The panel used up space, and closing it restored editing. That thread started on Photoshop CC 20.0.1, an older release, so treat the fix as a test rather than a rule. Try it when text editing freezes.
Check your Photoshop and macOS versions first

Text features change between releases. CG Channel reports that Photoshop 27.6, released in April 2026, added Dynamic Text. That update lets text flow around circles and curves. The same article lists macOS 14.0 or later as the requirement. An Apple Community thread about Photoshop 27.2 lists macOS 13 Ventura as the minimum, so the two sources do not agree. Check Adobe's system requirements page before you install, because this page could not confirm the answer from Adobe.

To find your build, follow [how to check your Photoshop version](/how-to/check-your-photoshop-version-in-photoshop). The version number tells you which text features you have, so check it before you follow any step that depends on a newer control.

Where Lazur fits when you get stuck

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac. Hold Option and Command together to ask about anything on screen. Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Ask where the Type tool is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it. Ask how to change the alignment, and Lazur guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click before it moves on.

Lazur does not click buttons or edit Photoshop for you. It points, explains and guides. It is not a plugin or add-in for Photoshop. If you want to speak your copy instead of typing it, hold fn to dictate. Dictation types clean text at the cursor in any app. Test it in a text layer first, so you know how it behaves before a deadline.
What to do after you add text

Save a layered PSD master before you export anything. Export a flattened PNG or JPEG for sharing, and keep the PSD as your working file. Name each text layer after the words it holds. That habit makes later edits faster. If the Type tool misbehaves after an update, read how to [reset preferences in Photoshop](/how-to/reset-preferences-in-photoshop). For more workflows, see [Photoshop for designers](/for/designers/photoshop).

faq.question: Can I add text in Photoshop on the web?
faq.answer: Adobe's Photoshop page says there is no free version on the web. Uploading your own photos on the web needs a paid plan or a free trial. The steps on this page cover the desktop app on a Mac, so check the web version separately.

faq.question: What is the keyboard shortcut for the Type tool in Photoshop on Mac?
faq.answer: Press T while the Photoshop window is active. The shortcut selects the Type tool without a trip to the toolbar. Press V to switch back to the Move tool when you want to drag the text.

faq.question: Why does my text run off the edge of the canvas?
faq.answer: You probably made point type, which keeps going on one line. Press Command+Z to undo. Then drag a box for paragraph text, or Option-click to set a fixed width and height so the words wrap inside it.

faq.question: How do I change the font after I finish typing?
faq.answer: Press T, then click the text layer in the Layers panel or click into the words. Select the characters you want to change, then pick a new font in the Options bar. You can also use Window > Character for the same change plus spacing controls.

faq.question: Does Lazur add the text for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur points at the Type tool, explains the Options bar and guides you one click at a time. It does not click or type into Photoshop on your behalf, so you still do each step yourself.

faq.question: Which Photoshop version does this page cover?
faq.answer: This page refers to Photoshop 27.6, which CG Channel reports was released in April 2026. The sources used here did not confirm later versions, so check your version and Adobe's release notes before you follow the steps.

faq.question: Is there a free trial for Photoshop?
faq.answer: Adobe's plans page lists a 7-day free trial for individual and student plans. It converts to a paid Creative Cloud membership after 7 days unless you cancel. The individual plan lists at US$22.99 per month on the annual plan, billed monthly. Check the plans page for current pricing.

task: Add text in Photoshop on Mac
appliesTo: Photoshop 27.6 desktop app on macOS (verify your version)
requirements: macOS 14.0 or later for Photoshop 27.6, per CG Channel (check Adobe's requirements)
A document already open in Photoshop
A keyboard with Command, Option and Shift keys

steps.name: Open your document
steps.text: Open the file in Photoshop. Choose File > Open, pick your image, and click Open. You can also drag the file onto the Photoshop icon in the Dock. Text needs an open document, so do this first.
steps.tip: Work on a copy of the file so the original stays untouched.

steps.name: Select the Type tool
steps.text: Press T to select the Type tool. You can also click the T icon in the left toolbar. The Options bar at the top of the window changes to show font and size controls once the tool is active.
steps.tip: If the Options bar does not appear, the Type tool is not active. Press T again.

steps.name: Choose point text or paragraph text
steps.text: Click once on the canvas for point text, which runs in a single line. Click and drag to draw a box for paragraph text, which wraps inside the box. Release the mouse to set the box. Option-click instead to type exact width and height numbers.
steps.tip: Point text is the safer default for titles and labels.

steps.name: Type your text
steps.text: Type the words. Press Return to start a new line in point text. In a paragraph box, the text wraps on its own, so press Return only when you want a new paragraph. Use the Delete key to remove a mistake.
steps.tip: Plain Return never commits the text. It only adds a line.

steps.name: Set the font, size and color
steps.text: With the text still active, use the Options bar. Choose a font family from the menu, pick a style, and enter a size in the size field. Click the color swatch to change the color. Select only some characters first if the change should touch part of the text.

steps.name: Open the Character panel
steps.text: Choose Window > Character to open the Character panel. It holds leading, kerning, tracking and baseline shift. Use it when the Options bar is not enough. Changes apply to the active text or the selected characters, so check what is highlighted first.
steps.tip: Leave the panel open on the side of the screen between edits.

steps.name: Align the text
steps.text: Press Command+Shift+L for left, Command+Shift+C for center or Command+Shift+R for right. Use these while the text is active. Alignment controls how each line sits inside the text box, which matters most for paragraph text.

steps.name: Commit the text
steps.text: Press Command+Return to commit. You can also click the check mark in the Options bar. Clicking elsewhere on the canvas, or switching to another tool or layer, also commits the text. Committing ends editing, so the text is ready to move.
steps.tip: Plain Return adds a line. It does not commit.

steps.name: Move the text layer
steps.text: Press V to pick the Move tool, then drag the text on the canvas. Hold Shift while you drag to constrain the movement to a straight line.

steps.name: Rotate or scale the text
steps.text: Choose Edit > Free Transform, or press ⌘T, with the text layer selected. Drag a corner handle to scale the text. Hold Shift while you drag a corner to keep the proportions. Press Return to apply the change, or Escape to cancel.

steps.name: Edit text later
steps.text: Select the text layer in the Layers panel. Press T, then click inside the words. Double-click the T thumbnail to select all text on that layer, then type to replace it. Five clicks inside the text also select it all, according to Julieanne Kost.
steps.tip: Open the Layers panel from Window > Layers if you cannot see it.

steps.name: Save a layered master
steps.text: Choose File > Save As and pick PSD as the format. A layered PSD keeps every text layer editable. Export a flattened PNG or JPEG for sharing, and keep the PSD as your master file.
steps.tip: Name the file with a version, such as poster-v2.psd, so you can roll back.

troubleshooting.problem: Return keeps adding lines and the text will not commit
troubleshooting.fix: Press Command+Return (⌘↩) to commit. Plain Return only starts a new line. You can also click the check mark in the Options bar.

troubleshooting.problem: Text runs off the canvas on a single line
troubleshooting.fix: You made point text. Press Command+Z to undo, then drag a box for paragraph text, or Option-click to set a fixed width and height so the words wrap.

troubleshooting.problem: The Type tool stops responding or the text layer will not edit
troubleshooting.fix: One Adobe Community thread reports that closing the Learn more about Photoshop side panel freed space and restored editing. That thread used Photoshop CC 20.0.1, so test this on a copy first.

troubleshooting.problem: Text stops being editable after you switch tools
troubleshooting.fix: Switching tools commits the text. Select the T layer in the Layers panel, press T, and click into the words to edit again.

troubleshooting.problem: Photoshop 27.6 may not run on your Mac
troubleshooting.fix: CG Channel lists macOS 14.0 or later for 27.6, but an Apple Community thread lists macOS 13 for 27.2. Check Adobe's requirements page before you update.
